we propose a novel feature descriptor, called local tetra patterns, for content-based image indexing and retrieval and show that it improves the retrieval result by 2.5%–6% as compared to the standard local binary pattern.

the development of a novel image retrieval algorithm for CBIR.
the development of an efficient CBIR system using the proposed method and the Gabor transform for the efficient retrieval of textured images.
developing a new image indexing and retrieval method for efficient and accurate retrieval of images from large image databases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method outperforms the LBP, LTP, and the derivative-based LBP methods in terms of average accuracy and computational complexity.
the proposed method has a better performance than the standard LBP, the LTP and the local derivative patterns (LDP) for texture image retrieval.
the proposed method is more effective and efficient than the existing methods for CBIR applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the local tetra patterns are a novel and efficient image descriptor that can be used for content-based image indexing and retrieval.

the local tetra pattern (LTrP) is a novel image feature descriptor which encodes the relationship of the referenced pixel and it's surrounding neighbors, based on directions calculated using first-order derivatives in horizontal and vertical directions.
we proposed a novel image indexing method for content-based image retrievals (CBIRs) using local tetra pattern (LTrP).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed LTrP descriptor is a simple yet effective texture descriptor that can be used for CBIR.
the local tetra patterns are more effective than the local ternary patterns in terms of average accuracy and average retrieval rate.

we can use the local tetra patterns to improve the retrieval result from the standard LBP, the LTP, and the local derivative patterns (LDP) in terms of average accuracy, precision, recall, and retrieval rate.
